title: The last ferry
goal: Read a literary passage closely, for its tenses, its rhythm and its narrator, and write a short scene in literary style.

intro.text: A literary paragraph uses everything in this unit at once: a base tense and its switches, long chains cut by a short sentence, words moved for rhythm, and a narrator who slips into a character's thoughts. Read slowly, and at each sentence ask: who is speaking now?

vocab.en: serial, instalment (tefrika edilmek: to be serialized)
about, concerning (after the dative; written: aşka dair bir roman)

exercises.title: Son vapur
exercises.passage:
Selin iskeleye vardığında hava kararmak üzereydi. Son vapur çoktan kalkmıştı. Banklardan birine oturup çantasını dizlerine koydu, uzun uzun denize baktı.

Ne yapacaktı şimdi? Annesi evde onu bekliyordu, belliydi; yemeği yine ısıtıp yine soğutacaktı. Telefonu çıkardı, sonra vazgeçip geri koydu. Ne diyecekti ki? Bir saattir arkadaşlarıyla gülüp eğlendiğini mi?

Martılar, sanki onunla alay edercesine, başının üstünde dönüp duruyordu. Birden ağlayası geldi. Ağlamadı. Kalktı, ceketine sıkıca sarınıp kıyı boyunca yürümeye başladı.

Derken arkasından bir motor sesi duyuldu. Döndü. Küçük bir tekne iskeleye yanaşıyor, yaşlı bir adam ona el sallıyor: “Karşıya mı, kızım?”

Selin bir an durdu. Sonra gülümsedi; gülümseyişi kendisini de şaşırttı. Karşıya, evet. Eve.

glossary.en: to heat up, to warm up
to mock, to make fun of (with -lA)
to come alongside, to pull in (dative)
the other side (here, of the Bosphorus: karşıya)

exercises.translation: When Selin reached the pier, it was about to get dark. The last ferry had long since left. She sat down on one of the benches, put her bag on her knees and looked at the sea for a long time. What was she going to do now? Her mother was waiting for her at home, that much was clear; she would heat up the dinner again and let it go cold again. She took out her phone, then changed her mind and put it back. What would she say, anyway? That she had been laughing and having fun with her friends for the last hour? The gulls kept circling above her head, as if mocking her. Suddenly she felt like crying. She didn't cry. She got up, wrapped herself tightly in her jacket and began to walk along the shore. And just then, the sound of an engine came from behind her. She turned. A small boat is pulling in at the pier, and an old man is waving to her: “Going across, dear?” Selin stopped for a moment. Then she smiled; her smile surprised even her. Across, yes. Home.

questions.q: Why do *yanaşıyor* and *sallıyor* switch to the present after *Derken*?
options: To bring the moment close: the historical present at the turning point
Because the boat comes every evening
Because Selin only heard about it later
questions.explain: *Derken* announces the turn; the present makes the boat's arrival happen before the reader's eyes.

questions.q: Whose words are *Ne diyecekti ki? Bir saattir arkadaşlarıyla gülüp eğlendiğini mi?*
options: Selin's thoughts, in the narrator's third person and past
Her mother's words on the phone
questions.explain: Free indirect speech: her own questions and her *ki*, with no quotation marks and no *diye düşündü*.

questions.q: What does *sanki onunla alay edercesine* add?
options: How the gulls seem to Selin: as if they were mocking her
That the gulls really attack her
questions.explain: *Sanki … -cAsInA*: an impression, coloured by her mood.

questions.q: What does the short sentence *Ağlamadı.* do after *Birden ağlayası geldi.*?
options: It cuts the rhythm and shows her holding back
questions.explain: A long sentence, a feeling, then two words: the rhythm does the work.

options: Selin's decision, in her own words, without diye
questions.explain: Free indirect speech again, reduced to the words she might say to herself.

exercises.prompt: Martılar, sanki onunla alay edercesine, başının üstünde dönüp duruyordu.
accept: The gulls kept circling above her head, as if mocking her.
The gulls kept circling above her head as if making fun of her
The gulls kept circling above her head as if to mock her
The gulls kept circling over her head as if [mocking|making fun of|to mock] her
The gulls kept wheeling [above|over] her head as if [mocking|making fun of|to mock] her
The gulls kept flying around [above|over] her head as if [mocking|making fun of|to mock] her
The seagulls kept [circling|wheeling|flying around] [above|over] her head as if [mocking|making fun of|to mock] her
Seagulls kept [circling|wheeling|flying around] [above|over] her head as if [mocking|making fun of|to mock] her
As if [mocking|making fun of] her, [the gulls|the seagulls|seagulls] kept [circling|wheeling|flying around] [above|over] her head
[The gulls|The seagulls] were circling [above|over] her head as if [mocking|making fun of] her
[The gulls|The seagulls] kept circling [above|over] her head as though [mocking|making fun of] her
exercises.explain: *Dönüp duruyordu* ([B2 unit 6](gp-ip-durmak)) is **kept circling**; *sanki … alay edercesine* is **as if mocking her**.

exercises.text: Uzun bir yolculuktan sonra eve döndüğünde ___ yorgundu.
exercises.en: When she came home after a long journey, she was dead tired.
exercises.explain: *Ölesiye* (to death) intensifies a state or an effort: *ölesiye yorgun*, *ölesiye çalışmak*. *Doyasıya* is for enjoying something fully: *doyasıya gülmek*.

exercises.prompt: Suddenly he felt like going back to his village.
accept: Birden köyüne dönesi geldi.
Birden köyüne geri dönesi geldi.
Aniden köyüne (geri) dönesi geldi.
[Birden|Aniden] köyüne (geri) dönmek istedi.
[Birden|Aniden] canı köyüne (geri) dönmek istedi.

reject.why: *Dönesim* is **I** felt like. For **he**, the possessive is in the third person: *dönesi geldi*.
The wish is what comes, so *gelmek* stays in the third person: *dönesi geldi*.

exercises.explain: *Dönesi geldi* is the literary way to say it; *dönmek istedi* and *canı dönmek istedi* are the everyday ones.

exercises.question: Which opening has an intrusive narrator who talks to the reader, as in the early Turkish novel?
options: Okuyucularım, size şimdi bir genç adamın hikâyesini anlatacağım.
Selin iskeleye vardığında hava kararmak üzereydi.

why.1: A hidden narrator: we see Selin, not the person telling the story.
why.2: Free indirect speech: Selin's own thought.

exercises.explain: Ahmet Mithat's narrator often stops the story to talk to his readers; Halit Ziya's stays out of sight (see the [interlude](c2-u02-culture)).

exercises.task: Translate the first sentence of Halit Ziya's *Aşk-ı Memnu* (1899–1900) into natural English, in one sentence. Glosses: *müsademe* collision, *andırmak* to resemble, *gene* again, *sıyırıp geçmek* to brush past.
exercises.source: Maun sandalla müsademeyi andıran bu tesadüflere artık o kadar alışmıştılar ki, bugün Kalender'den dönerken gene onun âdeta çarparcasına yakından sıyırıp geçişini fark etmemiş göründüler.
models: They had grown so used to these encounters, which were almost collisions with the mahogany boat, that today, on their way back from Kalender, they seemed not to notice it brush past them once again, so close it nearly struck them.
By now they were so used to these near-collisions with the mahogany boat that today, coming back from Kalender, they appeared not to notice it skimming past once more, as if it meant to ram them.
checklist: The pluperfect *alışmıştılar* comes out as **had grown used to** or **were used to by now**
*Çarparcasına* keeps its **as if to strike**, or **so close it nearly struck them**
*Fark etmemiş göründüler* is **seemed not to notice**, not **did not notice**: the women only pretend

exercises.text: Mektubu bir daha okudu. Demek her şey ___.
exercises.en: She read the letter once more. So it was all over.
exercises.explain: The ending happened before the reading, so the narrator's past moves to the pluperfect; *demek* is her own conclusion: *Demek her şey bitmişti.*

accept: He left. He never came back.
He left. He never came back again
He left. She never came back (again)
She left. [He|She] never came back (again)
[He|She] [left|went away]. [He|She] [did not|never] [come back|return] (again)
[He|She] [left|went away] and never came back
[He|She] left. And [he|she] never came back
exercises.explain: *Bir daha* after the verb lands on the end like a full stop; English needs no inversion to get the same weight.

exercises.en: Suddenly she felt like crying. She didn't cry.

exercises.task: Write a short scene of five to eight sentences in literary style. Use a base tense with one switch to the historical present, a chain with `-(y)Ip`, one form from this unit (*-(y)AsI gelmek*, `-cAsInA`, *doyasıya* or *ölesiye*) and at least one sentence of free indirect speech.
models: Kapıyı açtığında ev karanlıktı. Ceketini çıkarıp ışığı yaktı, mutfağa geçti. Masada bir not duruyordu. Okudu, bir daha okudu. Demek gitmişti. Birden ağlayası geldi. Ağlamadı; pencereyi açıp derin bir nefes aldı. Derken kapı çalıyor: karşısında, elinde bir demet çiçekle, kardeşi.

Bütün gün ölesiye çalışmıştı. Akşam olunca eve dönüp balkona çıktı, uzun uzun denize baktı. Martılar, sanki onu çağırırcasına, dönüp duruyordu. Neden bu kadar yorgundu? Bu iş ona ne vermişti ki? Derken telefon çalıyor; arayan, yıllardır görmediği bir arkadaşı.
checklist: One base tense (`-DI`) and a switch to the present at the turning point
One sentence of free indirect speech: a question or *demek*, without *diye düşündü*
Optional: a short sentence or a word after the verb for rhythm
